name: Axibase
tagline: HBase-backed time-series database with built-in SQL, rule engine and charts; withdrawn by Axibase in 2025.
description: Axibase Time Series Database (ATSD) was a Java time-series platform from Axibase Corporation aimed at IT infrastructure, industrial equipment and market data. It bundled a storage engine, SQL engine, rule engine for alerting, portal and charting library, REST and line-protocol network APIs, and a JDBC driver, and could ingest tcollector, Graphite, StatsD and OSIsoft PI formats or Kafka streams. A single node handled on the order of 200,000 metrics per second; scale-out mode ran on Apache HBase over HDFS, EMRFS or Azure Storage. The documentation stayed online until mid-2025, but the official Docker image was last updated in 2022 and axibase.com now says only that the company is 'operating in stealth mode', so ATSD should be treated as discontinued.
statusNote: ATSD docs and downloads removed in 2025; axibase.com now says the company operates in stealth mode. Last Docker image update was October 2022.

pricing.notes: Commercial editions were sold by Axibase; no longer offered.

scale.notes: Single node handled ~200k metrics/s; horizontal scale required deploying on HBase/HDFS.

strengths: All-in-one stack: storage, SQL, alerting rules and dashboards in one product
Accepted tcollector, Graphite, StatsD and OSIsoft PI ingestion formats
Automatic registration of new entities and metrics with no schema work
weaknesses: Product withdrawn; no support, updates or downloads
Scale-out depended on running and tuning HBase/HDFS
Proprietary with a small user community
useCases: Existing ATSD installations planning a migration
Historical reference for integrated TSDB-plus-alerting products
